why_the_simulator_cannot_reproduce_them: Both are verifier-side rejections caused by committed endpoint values failing the equality relation against the FFN's X/z16 planes. finish() deliberately performs NO equality precheck (zk_ffn_fresh_io.rs:274-275: 'No equality precheck: unequal committed values must fail the verifier's polynomial identity'), so a prover holding mismatched endpoints still emits a receipt and the verifier rejects. A simulator given only the statement (the two roots) cannot tell a matching witness from a mismatching one, so it cannot decide whether to output an accepting receipt or this rejection.

V_valid_relation_oracle_with_wrapper.matches: Faonio et al., Definition 8's S'_1 and Definition 9
V_valid_relation_oracle_with_wrapper.interface: S'_1(x, w) first checks (pp, x, w) in R, then runs and returns the output of S_1(x)
V_valid_relation_oracle_with_wrapper.covers: proof requests for valid statements; the witness-dependent rejections above never arise because invalid requests are refused by the wrapper before the simulator is invoked
V_valid_relation_oracle_with_wrapper.quote: Zero-knowledge is a security property that is only guaranteed for valid statements in the language, hence the above definition uses S'_1 as a proof simulation oracle.
V_valid_relation_oracle_with_wrapper.status: the right game for a ZK claim about this prover; still unproved here

wrapper_note: All three W-class predicates are part of the relation R: two are the endpoint equality relation and one is well-formedness of the caller's plane. In Game V the wrapper evaluates (pp, x, w) in R and refuses before the simulator is invoked, so the simulator never has to reproduce them. In Game A they are published as distinct error strings and leak.
